name: Fermented-fish noodles
summary: Bún mắm in Châu Đốc is the brown, clear, sweet fish broth VnExpress describes, eaten with roast pork and balut. The same article says the bowl is not only Châu Đốc: it is across the Mekong, adapted from a Cambodian bowl that used prohok. Da Nang’s bún mắm is a different bowl.
origin: Cambodia, then a Vietnamese adaptation, on VnExpress, 2 Oct 2019. The western bowl is cooked with cá linh instead of prohok.
taste: VnExpress says the broth looks brown from the mắm and is still clear, with a sweet fish taste.
howToEat: Eat it with roast pork and balut. VnExpress says many bowls also add shrimp, fish cake, and pork.
The herbs named are water-spinach tips, banana blossom, beansprouts, and fish mint.
The 26 Apr 2024 handbook lists bún mắm among the Mekong dishes inside Chợ Châu Đốc, with bún cá and lẩu mắm. The 20 Oct 2023 day names it for breakfast on the Hậu landing and at the market.
A bowl was printed at about 25,000–35,000 VND on 2 Oct 2019. Check on arrival.
where: Chợ Châu Đốc, and the Hậu landing at breakfast. VnExpress also says you can find the bowl in many Mekong towns. A house number was not printed. Check on arrival.
seoDescription: Bún mắm in Châu Đốc is a clear brown fermented-fish noodle with roast pork and balut. VnExpress says the bowl is eaten across the Mekong. Check on arrival.
